description: Replace the paragraph defining the class, including the existing tip exception.
old: The class $\Pext$ consists of the patterns in which: $\mathsf s$ is removed or has status $\mathrm D$ keeping two of its three bonds other than $\{y, \mathsf s\}$; each of $\mathsf e, \mathsf N, \mathsf W$ has status $\mathrm U$, $\mathrm X$, or $\mathrm D$ keeping the bond to $y$ and one other bond; each corner has status $\mathrm U$, $\mathrm X$, or $\mathrm D$ keeping two of its four bonds; and condition (C) holds for the bonds between non-removed sites of $\mathsf T(y)$ other than the tips. A pattern is straight or a turn according to $o$.

The two outside legs of each non-removed corner are filled with slots, whether or not they belong to its kept set. A pattern is straight or a turn according to $o$.

description: Replace the contraction/overflow sentence by the arithmetic justification.
old: The contraction is carried out in $64$-bit integer arithmetic, with run-time assertions that every entry stays below $2^{61}$.
new: The contraction is carried out in $64$-bit integer arithmetic, with binary64 shadow computations used for conservative overflow guards. The small integer moment tensors are first stored exactly in binary64 arrays and then converted to integers. Assume binary64 round-to-nearest arithmetic, let $u=2^{-53}$, $\gamma_{32}=32u/(1-32u)$, and $\eta=(1-u)^2(1-\gamma_{32})>1-10^{-12}>3/4$. Each contracted entry is a sum of at most sixteen nonnegative products, so its shadow $\widehat s$ and exact value $s$ satisfy $\widehat s\ge\eta s$ (two input conversions and at most thirty-two arithmetic roundings suffice). Thus a passing shadow guard $\widehat s<2^{61}$ implies $s<2^{61}/\eta$, and a sum of three such contraction entries is smaller than $2^{63}$. The subsequent shadow bounds for the current and next coefficient sums are computed from these nonnegative integer arrays; their passing threshold $2^{58}$ implies exact sums smaller than $2^{58}/\eta<2^{59}$. Consequently every accepted coefficient computation is free of integer overflow, including its intermediate sums.

description: Replace the restriction on floating-point use.
old: Floating-point arithmetic is used only for this choice.
new: Floating-point arithmetic is used for this choice, for the conservative overflow guards just described, and for diagnostics. Positivity is decided in unbounded integer arithmetic, and the closed-form tests use exact rational arithmetic.
